name: Nation-State APT Campaign
description: A sophisticated nation-state APT group has been conducting a long-term intrusion campaign. They have established multiple persistence mechanisms, created backdoor accounts, and are conducting stealthy data collection. Living-off-the-land techniques make detection very difficult.
objective: Identify and eradicate all APT footholds including backdoors, persistence mechanisms, and data collection staging areas. Assess the full scope of compromise.

events.message: Service account svc_backup logged in interactively on dc-server-01 at 03:22 AM — anomalous behavior
Scheduled task created: WindowsUpdateHelper runs C:\Windows\System32\upd_helper.exe daily at 4AM (SYSTEM)
DLL sideloading: legitimate winword.exe loading malicious version.dll from user profile directory
Low-frequency C2 beacon: dc-server-01 -> 45.142.212.200:443 every 3600 seconds (living-off-the-land using certutil)
Data staged for exfiltration: compressed archive created at C:\Windows\Temp\update_cache.zip (2.1GB)

hints: APT actors often use service accounts to blend in with normal traffic
Scheduled tasks and DLL sideloading provide persistent access across reboots
Low-frequency beacons are harder to detect — look for periodic connections
Check all hosts for staged data and unauthorized scheduled tasks
Assume multiple persistence mechanisms — find them all before declaring victory
